title: Squared CATE-Gradient Energy under Rough Observational Adjustment versus Fair Randomization

gap_reasons:
The stitched proofs close the pilot and likelihood dependencies, so the advertised matched rates and reference-law honesty obstruction are not conditional on the unresolved obligations in the earlier brief. The contribution remains confined to one dimension, smoothness configuration, known-design geometry and affine-centered neighborhood; it supplies no broader smoothness or dimensional phase diagram. Boundary-trace geometry is inherited from [Chen–Gao](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12673v3), and covariance correction is inherited from [Li et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3088168/), leaving the concentrated causal correction and common-target strip experiment as the substantive novelty. Exact finite-sample honesty follows through elementary risk calibration, while the fallback below 2^1024 and radius coefficient 2^600 make the supplied procedures existence certificates with uninformative intervals at ordinary sample sizes. The clinical examples concern different functionals and provide motivation without demonstrating usefulness of this energy benchmark; these scope and implementation limitations constrain the projected paper score despite fidelity of the matched-rate headline. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery constructed a total original-record pilot and attainers, matching risk and honest-length orders n^-6/31 observationally and n^-3/7 under supplied randomization, plus fixed-reference honesty penalty n^51/217. Two scoped D0 rounds closed the discovery obligations and tightened public constants; cold math and rubric reviews passed. D0.5 capped novelty at incremental (6.2 < 7.4); formalization never started and no Lean output, kernel verification, or substrate promotion was produced.
tldr: For squared causal CATE-gradient energy \(Q\) on the public uniform square, we prove matched original-record minimax absolute-risk and exactly finite-sample honest-length orders \(n^{-6/31}\) under rough observational adjustment and \(n^{-3/7}\) under supplied fair randomization. Both nuisance functions may have only H\"older exponent \(1/8\), the contrast has the fixed affine-centered closed-square \(C^3\) radius, and boundary derivatives are free. The total finite-computable procedures have explicit public error radii and coverage at least \(0.90\) at every sample size, with no necessary logarithmic multiplier. The common comparison constants are \((9/20)2^{-66}\) and \(2^{606}\). Concentrated boundary covariance correction, the retained nonlinear energy remainder, and a same-class full-support Bernoulli converse establish the frontier. Observational honesty costs order \(n^{51/217}\) even at the fixed randomized reference \(P_0\). This narrow precision benchmark concerns derivative explanations of continuous effect modification; it neither recomputes the ACTG175 TE-VIM analysis nor gives intervals for TE-VIM or LIFT-XAI's mean-absolute attribution score.
gap: Hall and Marron (1987) study the closer quadratic derivative functional in a density experiment. Unknown rough propensity and baseline regression, original Bernoulli observations, nonzero square-boundary flux, and observational-class honest length require separate analysis. Chen and Gao (2026), Example 8 and the quadratic-submanifold appendix, already cover boundary flux and nonlinear direct-regression traces. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (2024) cover pointwise smooth contrasts under rough confounding. Neither inspected result provides a uniformly calibrated gradient-energy procedure and converse for the specified original binary experiment.
fill: Determine all four precision orders on the specified classes, construct procedures with public numerical calibration at each sample size, and certify the converse in the same original-record experiment. The boundary identity is supporting geometry, rather than a novelty claim.
